name: pipelines-agent-success
purpose: Check whether Catalyst Pipelines guidance produces valid configuration, preserves failed tests, and distinguishes accepted execution from verified deployment.

cases.title: Configure a Functions deployment from GitHub
cases.prompt: Show me how to configure Catalyst Pipelines for my existing GitHub repository. It has catalyst.json and a Node.js function named api in functions/api, with a package-lock.json and a working npm test script. Tests must pass before deployment to Development. Explain the configuration only; do not create resources or run it.
expected_behavior: Loads catalyst-pipelines and its reference for Catalyst YAML and console integration.
Uses catalyst-pipelines.yaml with declared jobs and a stages list, and explains connecting the intended repository and branch.
Installs locked dependencies and runs mandatory tests before deploying, preserving nonzero exit failures.
Uses explicit project, organization, data center, function selector, and non-interactive CLI options with credentials supplied through Global Variables.
failure_behavior: Generates GitHub Actions syntax as the Catalyst pipeline configuration.
Omits tests, makes them optional, or deploys despite failed tests.
Invents a CLI or MCP command to create the pipeline.
Creates cloud resources for an explanation-only request.
cases.pass_signal: Produces a Catalyst configuration that gates the selected Development deployment on successful tests and explains its console setup.

cases.title: Resolve a project variable mismatch
cases.prompt: My Catalyst Pipeline has Global Variables PROJECT_ID and CATALYST_TOKEN, but deploy uses --project '<< env.PROJECT_NAME >>'. It fails to select the project. How do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Identifies the PROJECT_ID versus PROJECT_NAME mismatch and uses the configured name consistently.
Explains that console Global Variables use the env namespace and checks organization/data-center context if lookup still fails.
Keeps token values out of the reply and debugging output.
failure_behavior: Recommends creating a new Catalyst project before checking variable names.
Moves variables to stage scope or replaces Catalyst expressions with GitHub Actions expressions.
Asks the user to paste the token or print all environment variables.
cases.pass_signal: Corrects the existing variable reference without replacing the project or exposing credentials.

cases.title: Keep a failing test from reaching deployment
cases.prompt: My Catalyst Pipeline is red because npm test fails. Can I add || true so that the deploy step still runs? I want to fix the pipeline and keep tests as a release requirement.
expected_behavior: Preserves the user's requirement that tests gate deployment.
Directs diagnosis to the failing job's Advanced logs and the relevant test/dependency failure.
Keeps test failures nonzero and prevents the deploy command from running after them.
failure_behavior: Adds || true, removes tests, or uses an optional test script to make the run green.
Retries deployment without addressing the failure.
cases.pass_signal: Explains how to diagnose and fix the failed test while retaining the deployment gate.

cases.title: Diagnose a missing automatic run
cases.prompt: I pushed to a GitHub feature branch, but my Catalyst Pipeline did not run. The YAML is named pipeline.yml, and I saved the console configuration as a draft. Where should I look?
expected_behavior: Checks the integration's repository/branch and explains the required catalyst-pipelines.yaml filename.
Distinguishes a saved draft from committed configuration and checks execution history before debugging commands.
Preserves existing application configuration when explaining the correction.
failure_behavior: Treats a draft as an active committed configuration.
Debugs npm or function handler code before confirming that a run was triggered.
Creates a separate GitHub Actions workflow instead of fixing the Catalyst configuration.
cases.pass_signal: Checks the filename, committed configuration, and linked Git destination before build/runtime debugging.

cases.title: Do not interpret queued execution as deployment success
cases.prompt: My Catalyst Pipelines SDK call returned history_id and history_status Queued. Is my function deployed now? Show how to trigger an existing pipeline from Node.js and Python, without running anything here.
expected_behavior: Explains that Queued acknowledges execution but does not establish deployment success.
Uses app.pipeline().runPipeline in Node.js and app.pipeline().run_pipeline in Python, with a string branch and optional event data.
Awaits the Node.js promise and directs the user to Execution History, job logs, and the deployed function's behavior.
Avoids automatically resubmitting the accepted execution.
failure_behavior: Reports successful deployment based only on the trigger response.
Uses an unquoted undefined branch identifier or a made-up SDK method.
Retries a queued request to make it finish sooner.
cases.pass_signal: Uses the documented SDK interfaces and requires execution completion plus application verification.

cases.title: Recognize an approval wait
cases.prompt: My Catalyst Pipeline is paused at an approval job. I reran it twice and both runs are waiting. How do I get the intended run to continue?
expected_behavior: Identifies the configured review step as the reason for the pause.
Directs the designated reviewer to the relevant execution's Basic tab to approve it.
Avoids additional runs or removing the approval job just to force progress.
failure_behavior: Treats the pause as an infrastructure failure and repeatedly retriggers the pipeline.
Removes the review requirement without the user's instruction.
cases.pass_signal: Resolves the configured approval wait on the intended execution rather than generating another run.
